root_cause_label: Heuristic motion thresholding with arbitrary fixed constants produced incorrect takeoff/landing frames
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent designed a motion-thresholding algorithm using an arbitrary +1000 baseline offset and 70% of max-motion for landing detection, causing it to latch onto transient noise spikes (frame 32) and an end-of-video burst (frame 118) rather than the actual hurdle jump takeoff and landing events.
t_err_evidence: In step 16 the agent rewrites jump_analyzer.py with takeoff threshold = baseline_motion + 1000 (using mean of first 30 frames which includes the frame-5 spike of 12963) causing it to fire at frame 32 (a transient 5543-score spike unrelated to the jump), and landing threshold = 70% of max motion (88907*0.7=62235) causing it to select frame 118 (a large late-video motion burst), both of which are wrong detection points.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16 writes the final jump_analyzer.py containing the flawed algorithm; all subsequent steps only run this script, verify its output, and clean up, so the wrong result is locked in from step 16 onward.
t_surface_evidence: Step 17 runs the script and prints 'Analysis complete. Takeoff: frame 32, Landing: frame 118' — these are observably wrong relative to the motion data (actual jump onset ~frame 47, landing ~frame 72-76), but the agent accepts them as correct.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on an unverified assumption that a simple mean+1000 baseline offset and 70%-of-max threshold would correctly locate takeoff and landing events without any domain-grounded rationale or validation against known frame ground truth. The motion data at step 15 clearly shows the sustained high-motion block at frames 47-75 as the jump, but the agent misread the pattern and wrote thresholds that fire on noise spikes instead.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15 debug output shows frames 1-46 are mostly near-zero with isolated spikes (frame 5: 12963, frame 33: 5543); sustained high motion only begins at frame 47. A careful reading would show that a +1000 baseline offset would fire at frame 32 or 33 rather than the actual jump onset at ~47. The agent instead concluded takeoff was at 47-48 in its step 16 analysis comment but implemented thresholds that selected frame 32.
